cards.text: This is a psalm of David, and wicked and deceitful mouths are speaking lies against him. It's like finding a group chat that's ALL about you, and every single message is a lie. So David prays, “O God of my praise, be not silent.”

cards.question: These lying mouths surround David with hateful words and attack him. What reason does David say they have?
In return for David's ___, they accuse him.

cards.text: David's answer to all of it: “I am a man of prayer.” They repay him evil for good and hatred for his love, which is like baking somebody a WHOLE batch and getting the empty box thrown back at your head.
Then the psalm suddenly turns. It stops talking about “they” and starts praying about one man, “him,” and friend, buckle up.

cards.question: The prayer asks for a wicked man to be set over this man. Who should stand at his right hand?
When this man is tried, the prayer asks that he be found ___.

cards.text: May his days be few, and may another take his position. Then it reaches his family: his wife a widow, his children fatherless and wandering as beggars far from their ruined homes.

cards.question: The prayer comes for this man's belongings next. What should happen to all he owns?
The prayer asks that someone show favor to this man's fatherless children.

cards.text: It reaches down the generations: may his descendants be cut off and their name blotted out. May his fathers' iniquity and his mother's sin stay before the LORD.

cards.question: The prayer asks that no one show this man kindness. The reason given is that he never ___ kindness himself.

cards.text: And it gets worse. He pursued the poor and needy and brokenhearted, even to their death.

cards.question: This man loved cursing and refused to delight in blessing. What does the prayer ask?

answers.text: That cursing fall on him and blessing stay far away
That he finally learn to delight in blessing
That all his cursing be forgiven and forgotten

cards.text: Then comes a picture: he wore cursing like a coat, and the prayer asks it to soak into his body like water and into his bones like oil. I've worn this apron so long it's basically part of me, and that's the idea here, except it's cursing.

cards.question: The prayer pictures this man's cursing like a belt tied around him forever.

cards.text: Then David ties the whole thing together. He asks that all of this be the LORD's reward to certain people.

cards.question: Who does David ask the LORD to repay this way?

answers.text: His accusers who speak evil against him
Everyone in Israel who breaks the law
The nations that march against Israel

cards.text: Then David turns back to God, and the whole tone changes: “But You, O GOD, the Lord, deal kindly with me for the sake of Your name; deliver me by the goodness of Your loving devotion.”

cards.question: David asks God to deliver him. What reason does David give about himself?

cards.text: David says he's fading away like a lengthening shadow, his knees weak from fasting, his body lean and gaunt. Friend, I know fading: after years in that junk drawer, I was basically dust with a mustache.

cards.question: When David's accusers see him this weak, they rush over to help him.

cards.text: So David cries out again: “Help me, O LORD my God; save me according to Your loving devotion.”

cards.question: When God saves David, what does David want his accusers to know?

answers.text: That the LORD has done it
That David is stronger than them

cards.question: David tells God that even though his accusers curse, “You will ___.”

cards.text: When they rise up, David says, they will be put to shame, but Your servant will rejoice. They stand up to come at him, and HE'S the one rejoicing? Love it.

cards.question: Earlier, the wicked man wore cursing like a coat. Now David prays, “May my accusers be clothed with ___; may they wear their ___ like a robe.”

cards.text: Remember how David opened, asking God not to be silent? Now David makes a promise about his own mouth.

cards.question: David promises to praise the LORD quietly where no one else can hear.

cards.text: Then David gives the reason he's so sure. And it's a good one.

cards.question: Earlier, the prayer asked for an accuser at the wicked man's right hand. Who does David say stands at the right hand of the needy one?

cards.text: He's there to save him from the condemners of his soul. David starts out surrounded with hateful words and ends with the LORD right at his side, and friend, I'd take that trade EVERY single time.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 quotes "May my accusers be clothed with ___; may they wear their ___ like a robe.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The second half of verse 7, 'may his prayer be regarded as sin,' is never told on any card. It is a striking part of the curse, and the baker leaves Prep without ever meeting it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This card is the BSB wording of verses 8-10 with no quotation marks and no speaker. 'May his days be few, and may another take his position' reads as if Papa Dorin is wishing this on someone himself. It also has none of his voice. Frame it as what the prayer asks, the way cards 6, 7 and 9 do.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question says verse 16 is the reason for the request in verse 12 that no one show him kindness. Verse 16's 'For' follows verses 13-15. It doesn't point to verse 12 in particular, so the card makes a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The true or false answer is False, and no card ever says what the accusers actually do in verse 25. They scorn David and shake their heads when they see him. The baker only learns what they don't do.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This card uses the BSB words of verse 28 without quotation marks: 'they will be put to shame, but Your servant will rejoice.' Without quotes, 'Your servant' reads as if Papa Dorin is talking to the baker, and the moment doesn't make sense. Either quote the exact BSB wording or paraphrase it, for example 'but David, the LORD's servant, will rejoice.'

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The setup says 'the wicked man wore cursing like a coat.' In verse 18, the one who wore cursing is 'he,' the man being prayed against. The 'wicked man' in verse 6 is a different person, the one set over him.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The right answers for the two blanks are 'disgrace' and 'shame,' which mean nearly the same thing. They fit either blank equally well, so the only way to get the order right is to know the exact wording of the line. That makes the card a guess at wording, not a test of meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The setup says the prayer asked for an accuser 'at the wicked man's right hand.' Verse 6 asks for an accuser at the right hand of 'him,' the man being prayed against. The wicked man is the one set over him. The right hand in verse 6 isn't the wicked man's.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
